title: rrs, eis, and the injectables
dek: Amikacin/kanamycin: rrs 1401 a>g is the canonical 16S hit; eis promoter-up acetylates kanamycin (and can nudge AMK). Capreomycin additionally cares about tlyA. Historical drugs, still in genomes.
story: Second-line injectables are no longer preferred WHO therapy, but they remain salvage and they remain in BAMs. 16S rRNA rrs a1401g (E. coli 1408-adjacent numbering fights happen — state Mtb rrs coordinates) confers high-level kanamycin/amikacin resistance and often capreomycin. g1484t is a sibling allele.

eis promoter mutations (c-14t, g-10a, …) overexpress Eis aminoglycoside acetyltransferase. That is primarily a kanamycin story; amikacin may shift less. L2/Beijing has a higher prior on some eis promoters — lineage as covariate, still grade the allele.

tlyA loss-of-function blocks 16S/23S methylation needed for capreomycin (and viomycin) binding. Cross-resistance Venn: rrs 1401 hits the broad injectable set; eis is KAN-leaning; tlyA is CAP-leaning. Draw it before recycling an old injectable.
deepTitle: Streptomycin is a different rpsL/rrs/gid story
deep: Streptomycin: rpsL K43R/K88R, rrs 514/517 region, gid loss-of-function. Not interchangeable with AMK genetics.
Because injectables left Group A, rrs 1401 no longer defines XDR. It still defines “do not give AMK.”
Ototoxicity is the host reason they left, not a bacterial gene.
Numbering wars between E. coli 16S and Mtb rrs are how 1401 becomes 1408 in a report. Pick one and label it.

visual.caption: Injectable genetics are a Venn diagram. rrs 1401 is the broad 16S hit; eis is KAN-weighted; tlyA is CAP-weighted; streptomycin lives on rpsL/gid.

example.title: eis c-14t, need an injectable salvage
example.setup: Pre-XDR, BPaL failed, someone wants amikacin. WGS: eis c-14t, rrs WT, tlyA WT.

steps.title: AMK is not automatically dead
steps.body: Shift may be smaller. MIC the AMK; do not assume rrs-level resistance.

steps.title: CAP is a different Venn slice
steps.body: tlyA WT, rrs WT: CAP might still be on the table genetically — toxicity and WHO rank are separate objections.
